title: Hearing on federal immigration crackdowns hurting NYC businesses
summary: The Council's Small Business and Immigration Committees will examine how federal immigration enforcement and policy changes since 2025 are affecting New York City's economy and immigrant-owned businesses. Officials from the Department of Small Business Services and the Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs, along with advocates, are invited to testify about impacts such as declining foot traffic in immigrant neighborhoods, ICE raids, and new federal fees and restrictions on visas and loans. The briefing paper cites data on immigrant workers and taxpayers, including roughly 470,100 undocumented workers in New York State and a new $100,000 fee on H-1B visa petitions imposed in September 2025.
